domain: energy infrastructure safety - regulatory significance classification of reported pipeline incidents (Canada, federal)
prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source would support (parked, not taken to construction): when an incident is reported to the CER on a federally-regulated pipeline or facility, will the CER ultimately classify it 'Significant'? Honest report-time features: reported date, company, province, nearest populated centre, substance carried. The strongest columns (Incident Types, Release Type, Approximate Volume Released) are label-adjacent and would have to be excluded.
prediction_time: Would be the incident's report to the CER (Reported Date). The 'Significant' classification is the CER's post-assessment determination, so the label genuinely post-dates the instant - the timing contract is the one clean thing about this source.
target_definition: Would be binary: Significant = yes/no (data dictionary: 'Whether the incident is a significant incident, which is an acute event that results in: -death; -a serious injury (as defined in the OPR); -a fire or explosion that causes a pipeline or facility to be inoperative; -a LVP hydrocarbon release in excess of...' - i.e. mechanically derived from consequence fields that cannot ship as features).

split_strategy: Measured on the full file (2,034 rows, 2008-2026): rows/year 52-173; Significant=yes per year 6-51, both classes in every one of the 19 years; total positives 361 (17.75%). Windows would be e.g. train 2008-2019 (~1,235 rows, ~177 positives), eval 2020-2022 (~380, ~98), holdout 2023-2026 (~385, ~126) - the split contract is satisfiable. The blocker is below, not the splits.

measurements.panel_2026_10_21: probe_download_measure.py over pipeline-incidents-data.csv: 2,034 rows x 16 columns, years 2008-2026, Significant 361/2,034 = 17.75%; Status: Closed 2,002, Submitted 15, Initially Submitted 17; Incident Types distribution: 'Release of Substance' 810, 'Operation Beyond Design Limits' 499, 'Fire' 446, 'Serious Injury (as defined in the OPR)' 125, 'Adverse Environmental Effects' 80, 'Fatality' 7 (combinations rarer); Substance: 'Not Applicable' 1,188, 'Natural Gas - Sweet' 559, crude/propane/NGL etc; Release Type: 'Not Applicable' 1,188, Gas 673, Liquid 97. Volume released (m3): n=594 numeric, median 19.3, >=1 m3: 479, >=10: 330, >=100: 233.
measurements.honest_feature_auc_measured: In-sample single-categorical AUC vs Significant (levels with >=5 rows; measured, in-sample, no holdout - recorded to show the signal that survives the timing exclusion): Company 0.7295 (26 levels), Province 0.7015 (9), Substance 0.6585 (19), Year 0.6526 (19), Release Type 0.5294 (4). Label-adjacent Incident Types alone: 0.9143 - the strongest column is the one that cannot ship.
measurements.label_mechanics: The data dictionary defines Significant mechanically from consequences (death; serious injury as defined in the OPR; fire/explosion rendering pipeline/facility inoperative; LVP hydrocarbon release above threshold) - i.e. the label is a deterministic function of consequence fields (Incident Types, volume) that are excluded as post-hoc/label-adjacent. A solver never sees the information the CER used.
measurements.cost_measured: 3.0 MB across 3 files in 6.5 s, anonymous, from the coordinator - trivially cheap access; monthly-ish update cadence implied by last-modified 2026-10-01.

rejection_reason: PARKED on task shape, not access or licence (both clean, measured): (1) the label is mechanically derived from consequence fields that cannot ship, so the honest report-time feature set collapses to company/province/substance/date, and the measured in-sample AUC of the best honest column (Company, 0.73) shows the task is mostly operator risk profiling; (2) only 2,034 rows and ~180 positives total across 19 years - thin for a scored eval; (3) it is the same 'predict the regulator's classification of a reported event' family as the existing hc-recalls-classification candidate, in the same jurisdiction, with weaker data. Prior art comparison: PHMSA's US pipeline-incident data (raw, Kaggle-visible) and CER's own viewer exist, but no public ML-ready pipeline-incident significance benchmark was found - so this is not a mirror verdict; it is a marginal-task park.
next_action: Parked. Unpark only if: (1) a formulation is wanted that ships the company's initial notification free text with verified timing (the comprehensive file's 'Detailed what happened' is likely post-investigation - timing would need evidence), or (2) the operator explicitly wants a small regulator-classification task despite the operator-profiling ceiling, or (3) CER's data is re-probed and the comprehensive file turns out to carry report-time fields that materially widen the honest feature set. Re-measure honest-feature AUC before any construction.
